title: Book Two · Chapter 82: The Open Door on the Left
story:
In October, the reading group has a short task in the school yard. Miss Wu gives each pair a card. They must find a place. They must read the notice there. Then they must bring back one answer.

Ronan works with a quiet child from another row. Jun has his own partner. Leo and Mei receive different cards.

Ronan reads his card. First, stand at the garden gate. Then face the main building. Look to the left. The answer is on an open door.

He reads left and points toward the small trees. His partner looks at the first line again.

“We start at the gate.”

“I know.”

Ronan walks to the gate. From here, the building is in front of him. The left side is now the other side of the yard. He turns halfway, then stops.

His partner puts both feet toward the building.

“Like this.”

Ronan stands beside him. Now they point to the same door. It is open. A paper hangs just inside.

They do not reach for the answer yet. Ronan looks at the first line of the card again.

“From the gate,” he says.

His partner nods.

Ronan puts one hand toward the small trees. From their old place, that seemed like the left side. Here, his arm points away from the door.

He lowers it and faces the building properly.

The other child waits beside him instead of pulling him along the path. Ronan reads the next line aloud.

“Look to the left.”

Both turn their heads. This time, he does not have to copy the other child's hand.

A child from another pair passes with a different card. Ronan nearly follows, then checks his own words.

“Our door is here.”

His partner smiles and moves toward it with him. The answer will come from the notice inside, after they have reached the right place.

They walk along the clear path. The notice asks children to leave wet umbrellas outside the room. There is a stand beside the step. Their card asks for the place for umbrellas. Ronan writes stand beside the step.

Back at the table, he draws a quick line from the gate. He wants to show the direction. But on the paper, his left turn goes toward the wrong corner again.

Ronan turns his paper. He puts the gate on the paper nearest to him. The building is above the gate. Then he draws the turn. His partner watches and nods.

Miss Wu checks their answer. She asks both children to point to the real door. They do. Then she gives them a new line to read in the classroom.

The outdoor task is over. They do not make a guide for other children. Ronan puts his card back in the teacher's pile with the others.

At lunch, Jun asks about their task. “Which place did you find?” Ronan tells him about the umbrella stand. Jun's card led to a notice beside the water tap.

“Was yours easy?”

“After I faced the right way.”

Jun turns around on the spot. “Now left is over there.”

Ronan turns with him. They are standing face to face. For a moment, both point in different directions.

Leo comes between them with the ball.

“Can left wait?” he asks.

They go to the open part of the yard. This time, the direction is simple. The ball is in front of them. All three run toward it at once.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

left＝左边；gate＝大门；notice＝通知。

## 理解问题

1. 小组这次实际要读什么？
2. Ronan怎样解决左右方向的困惑？

## 读句子

**Ronan / turns / his paper.** Ronan／转动／他的纸。
